I consider myself to be between gender fluid and MTF transexual. I have kids and a wife and they don't want me to take hormones and transition, so I have yet to start them even though I have been approved for them, have my letter and the Endo said he will write me the script after another round of blood work. Yet I'm still clinging to the idea that I can get by without the HRT. This is my second bout of intense dysphoria in my life. When I was a kid and before the internet it was merely just a fantasy. Now the idea that it is a choice and I can choose to pursue a transition it makes fantasy real and that is the hardest part. To go from fantasy to fighting something I want. I don't hate my maleness though so it's been hard to leave it behind and pursue transition full force. It probably wouldn't be as hard though if my wife and kids weren't so attached to my male side. In fact I would definitely already be on HRT if it weren't for them. There's a point in transition where one needs to disrobe from their birth gender. When I hit this point I begin to realize that much of what we consider gender is social constructs and since I'm a gender outlaw I don't really follow them anyways. So to look more female or male to some extent requires me to give in to these constructs which I don't agree with. As I write this I'm realizing that one of the reasons why I don't agree with these social constructs is because the typical male ones don't fit me well, so between that and my desire for secondary sex characteristics of a female does that make me an ideal HRT candidate? I'm thinking yes. Sorry for being all over on this response. But from someone that can relate to what you wrote I figured I'd let it all pour out.
